name: The Augmentation Debt Crisis: When Chrome Becomes a Chain
author: GLMZ Financial Stability Council
body:
Augmentation debt is the fastest-growing category of consumer debt in the GLMZ. Total outstanding augmentation loans exceed Φ800 billion. 34% of augmented individuals in Tier 1-3 carry some form of augmentation debt. The average repayment period is 15 years. The default rate is 22%.

The debt structure is uniquely punitive because of SNT's properties:

1. You cannot return the product. Once SNT bonds an implant to your body, removal is a major surgical procedure with significant health risks and psychological consequences. There is no 'returns policy' for chrome.

2. You cannot stop paying without consequences. SNT maintenance is required every 8-12 years. If you default on your augmentation loan, the financing corponation may deny SNT maintenance. Your bonding layer degrades. Your implant fails. You experience phantom chrome syndrome. You are, effectively, punished with chronic pain and disability for being poor.

3. The debt follows you across jurisdictions. Unlike criminal records, which are jurisdiction-specific, financial obligations are tracked through the Inter-Corporate Credit Bureau — one of the few databases that IS shared between corponations, because debt collection serves everyone's interests.

The result is a population of augmented poor who took on debt to become functional in an economy that increasingly requires augmentation for employment, and who now cannot escape the debt because the product is permanently attached to their bodies.

The Burden Clause — a provision in the Gradient Compact that prohibits debt bondage — has been cited in legal challenges to augmentation debt practices. These challenges have failed. The courts have held that denying SNT maintenance is not bondage because the debtor is 'free to seek maintenance from alternative providers.' Alternative providers do not exist at prices the debtor can afford. Freedom to seek alternatives that do not exist is not freedom.
